title: Affine-invariant Cubic Newton with Weak Learners
claim: Second-order weak-learner edges stay well above theoretical lower bounds in practice, and remain comparable to or better than first-order edges as training proceeds.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared y-axis, edges vs iteration and vs loss
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the y-axis label 'Weak Learner Edge', which ranges from 0 to 0.4. The left panel plots edge against tree boosting iteration (0 to 500). The right panel plots edge against loss value on a log-scaled axis. Three methods are shown in blue (GRN γ_k), orange (AICN Θ_k) and green (Gradient Θ_k^E). Solid lines are running averages and dashed lines are running infima. Faint noisy traces show the raw per-iteration values. A dotted black horizontal line at about 0.04 marks the expected lower bound. In the left panel, the green average curve sits well above the blue and orange curves, which nearly overlap. The infima step down toward the dotted line. In the right panel, the edges rise steeply as loss increases. Legends sit in the top of each panel.
caption: Comparison of weak learner edges for tree boosting on HIGGS ($n=10000,\ J=4$): Hessian cosine angle $\Theta_k$ for weak-AICN, weak gradient edge $\gamma_k$ for weak-GRN, and Euclidean cosine angle $\Theta_k^E$ for first-order boosting. Left: Edges against boosting iterations. Right: Edges against training loss. Solid lines show arithmetic running averages; dashed lines show running infima. The dotted line shows the proxy expectation lower bound from [ref] as a reference value.
abstract: Modern gradient boosting algorithms are based on Newton's method, which excels empirically but lacks global convergence guarantees. While recent work on Gradient-Regularized Newton (GRN) boosting achieved a global $\mathcal{O}(1/Î³^{12}k^2)$ rate, its analysis was not able to exploit the natural Hessian geometry and suffers from a heavy $Î³^{12}$ dependence on a worst-case `weak gradient edge' $Î³$. In this paper, we tackle these theoretical drawbacks by generalizing the Affine-Invariant Cubic Newton (AICN) scheme to convex optimization with weak learners. Our analysis is based on average cosine values $\overlineÎ_k$ along the optimization path and directional improvements $Î´_k$ in the Hessian-induced norm. We show that the weak-AICN update reduces to a damped weak-Newton step with an explicit stepsize determined by $Î´_k$. Under semi-strong self-concordance, we establish a global $\mathcal{O}(1/\overlineÎ_k^4 k^2)$ rate, significantly improving upon the weak-GRN bound. We further prove a local linear rate, global linear convergence for Hessian-dominated losses, cosine angle lower bounds, and present weak-AdaAICN, which adaptively tunes the cubic regularization. Finally, we demonstrate the broader applicability of this framework beyond gradient boosting by showing that Newton coordinate descent emerges naturally as a special case of optimization with weak learners.
